definitions.explanation: A game or activity where one shoots at targets, especially the cork-gun shooting stalls found at Japanese festivals and hot spring towns.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{祭|まつ}り→お祭り：01349_omatsuri⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{射的|しゃてき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I played the shooting gallery at the festival.

examples.japanese: {射的|しゃてき}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{景品|けいひん}→景品：08319_keihin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{当|あ}てた→当てる：01864_ateru⟧。
examples.english: I won a big prize at the shooting gallery.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ころ→〜ころ：03091_koro⟧、⟦{温泉|おんせん}{街|がい}→温泉街：09228_onsengai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{射的|しゃてき}⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{楽|たの}しみ→楽しみ：01651_tanoshimi⟧だった。
examples.english: When I was a child, I looked forward to going to the shooting gallery in the hot spring town.

notes:
In Japan, {射的|しゃてき} most commonly refers to the cork-gun shooting game found at summer festivals (⟦{夏祭|なつまつ}り→夏祭り：09871_natsumatsuri⟧), shrine festivals, and ⟦{温泉|おんせん}{街|がい}→温泉街：09228_onsengai⟧ (hot spring towns). Players use a cork gun to try to knock down prizes displayed on shelves. It is a nostalgic pastime associated with traditional Japanese entertainment.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {射的|しゃてき}⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧: shooting gallery stall
- {射的|しゃてき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to play the shooting game
- {射的|しゃてき}{場|じょう}: shooting range
- {射的|しゃてき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{景品|けいひん}→景品：08319_keihin⟧: shooting gallery prizes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {的当|まとあ}て: target game — a broader term for any hit-the-target game
- ⟦{射撃|しゃげき}→射撃：16089_shageki⟧: shooting — the serious sport or military activity, not a game
